misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program SaringKataPanjang
kamus
  n, m, i, panjangKata : integer
  kata : string
algoritma
  input(n, m)
  i <- 1
  if i <= m then
    input(kata)
    panjangKata <- panjang(kata)
    if panjangKata > n then
      output(kata)
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with an if-statement, believing that the if-statement will repeatedly execute its body as long as the condition `i < len(txt)` remains true. They expect the if-statement to behave like a while loop, incrementing i and checking each word in the list until i reaches len(txt). In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so only the first word (at index 0) is checked, and i is incremented to 1 but never used again. The function will only return at most one word instead of all words longer than n characters.
